subject: AureaCare — temporary pinning window and evidence for cross-region processing
messages:
From: Julie Wang <julie.wang@aureacare.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security@aureacare.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency confirmation + temporary cross-region processing window

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we move forward with a contract, our security team needs explicit confirmation on two operational items that are blockers for our vendor review:

1) Region pinning for APAC customer data: we need a contractual commitment that customer data will be pinned to APAC compute and storage for primary processing. Please confirm which APAC regions you support (Tokyo, Osaka, Singapore) and whether embedding vectors derived from PII will ever be materialized outside APAC under normal operation.

2) Temporary cross-region processing windows: we understand that transient failover or service resilience can cause brief cross-region hops. Our security policy allows this only for documented incidents and only up to 3 hours per incident with audit evidence. Can you provide a playbook or evidence describing: detection, allowed duration, audit logs, and post-incident notification cadence?

If you can provide a short annex or evidence pack (network map, subprocessor roster, and an example audit log entry), we can move to legal redlines next week.

Best,
Julie Wang
Head of Security Operations
AureaCare

--
AureaCare security@aureacare.com
From: sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com

Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + temporary cross-region processing window

Hi Julie—

Thanks for the clear ask. Summary answers up front:
- APAC regions supported: ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo), ap-northeast-3 (Osaka), ap-southeast-1 (Singapore). You can pin projects to any of these regions for both storage and compute; by default we pin embeddings and models to the selected region.
- Under normal steady-state operations, embedding vectors and model inference outputs are retained and processed only in the pinned region.
- For transient resilience/failover, our standard playbook allows a temporary hop to an equivalent APAC region or to our control-plane region for up to 4 hours per incident, with automated telemetry and an incident report.

Notes: I flagged the 4-hour window because our current resilience SLOs are built around a 4-hour escalation and rollback cycle for isolated kernel maintenance and autoscaling migrations. That said, we can discuss tightening this to 3 hours for AureaCare if the legal and ops teams agree to the compensating controls (additional pre-warming, reserved capacity for critical projects).

I attached: Redwood_DPA_Annex_AureaCare_v1.pdf (draft annex with pinning language), transient-egress-playbook-72h.csv (runbook outline + example log row). The playbook includes the detection signals we emit and the audit entry schema.

Would you be able to confirm whether AureaCare requires a hard contractual cap of 3 hours, or whether a 3-hour target with operational mitigations is acceptable? If you need a sample audit log, I can share one redacted example immediately.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Security PM — Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): Redwood_DPA_Annex_AureaCare_v1.pdf (pdf), transient-egress-playbook-72h.csv (text)

Kim / Sofia / Neha —

I pulled a redacted audit line and validated the detection fields. Summary: we emit a single-line JSON audit record for any transient-hop event with these fields: event_id, start_ts, end_ts, source_region, target_region, reason_code, trigger_signal, impacted_project_id. The example I extracted (redacted) shows a 00:45 duration for a planned autoscaler migration between ap-northeast-1 -> ap-northeast-3; retained vector storage remained pinned and only runtime cache warmed in target region.

Recommendation:
- For AureaCare, to accept a 3-hour hard contractual cap we should require reserved capacity (small dedicated pool) for the pinned project so we avoid autoscaler-induced cross-hops. That is a billable item.
- If legal prefers Annex language, we can add Section A.2—"Temporary Resilience Hop"—that requires: (a) customer opt-in for reserved capacity OR (b) explicit acceptance of operational target (3 hours) with automated incident reporting and a post-incident RCA within 48 hours.

I attached the redacted example to this thread for Sofia to share with the customer as evidence if we get a sign-off on Annex language.

Karthik
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
